newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for May 7.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for May 7.

text.p: Mexican crude port Dos Bocas reopened at 0640 local/1140 GMT Wednesday to crude exports, Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1000 local/1500 GMT daily meteorological report.

The Gulf of Mexico port originally shut on Saturday afternoon, reopened at 1825 local Monday and closed again at 0615 local Tuesday to crude exports. Tugboats that guide the tankers could not operate because of waves eight to ten feet high, a port official told Reuters.
A regional cold front has relaxed in intensity since the weekend.
Salina Cruz port in Oaxaca remained closed to smaller ships, such as tourism and fishing craft, amid winds 48 km per hour, the report said.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.

Some clouds and possible rains along northern Baja California peninsula, winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 29 km/11 to 16 miles per hour) with waves three to six feet high. Isolated electric storms along Oaxaca and Chiapas coasts.
Mostly clear skies and winds from 10 to 15 knots.
Hot and clear to partly cloudy with winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
